13:The right sidebar's Tasks tab: every task of the project at a glance, what has run, what is running, and what is queued, where any of them can be looked into, edited, and adjusted, and a chain given more steps.
17:The tab is one scrolling column, with a [Scrollbar](../../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar), read top to bottom as a timeline, in three groups, each headed by a small muted label with its count: "Previous", every task that has run, oldest at the top, as the [PromptEditor](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s previous tasks are, with their filters and batch actions along the group's heading; "Running", every task under way, in either lane; and "Queued", the queue, in its order, as the [QueueList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says, reordered by dragging, its auto-send switch and "Send next" button along its heading. A group with nothing in it shows its heading alone, muted, "No queued prompts" and the like.
18:Every level of the tab remembers where it was scrolled, and coming back to it, however, finds it just as it was left. The list keeps its scroll when a task is opened from it and the back arrow or <Escape> returns to it, when the sidebar slides back and out again, when it is closed and opened by hand, and when another project is shown and this one shown again, each open project keeping its own. Each open task keeps its own scroll, its Prompt expanded or clipped, and its Steps section as it was, for as long as the application runs, so opening it again, from the list, a step of its chain, View all, or anywhere else, shows it where it was left; going from a chain to one of its steps and back returns to the chain where it was. The list is scrolled on its own only the first time it is shown for a project in a launch, so the Running section, or the start of the Queued one when nothing runs, is in view, and when a task is opened from elsewhere, as from the running activity list, which scrolls it into view. Rows added, removed, or moved above what is in view, as tasks finish and move from Running to Previous, never shift the rows in view: the scroll is kept on the row at the top of the view, not on a number of pixels. The three groups are accordion sections, each collapsible on its own. A section's heading is a row 28 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface, a step apart from the rows: a chevron at its left, pointing right while collapsed and down while expanded, then its title and count, then, at its right, its own controls, Previous's filter and batch actions and Queued's auto-send switch and "Send next". Clicking the heading, anywhere but its controls, expands or collapses that section alone; any number can be expanded at once, and collapsing one takes its rows away and leaves only its heading. Previous starts collapsed and Running and Queued expanded, each time a project is opened; otherwise each stays as it was left while the application runs, each open project keeping its own. A collapsed section still counts its tasks, its controls still work, and opening one of its tasks from elsewhere, as from the running activity list, expands it to show that task.
19:All three headings are always in view, however far the tab is scrolled, so each section's controls are always in reach. A heading whose section starts above the visible rows is pinned at the top of the tab, and one whose section starts below them is pinned at its bottom, in their order: scrolled down into Running, the Previous heading is pinned at the top, the Running heading beneath it, and the Queued heading at the bottom; scrolled into Queued, Previous and Running are pinned at the top, one beneath the other. A heading never pushes another out of view; they stack, each 28 pixels, so the rows scroll in the space left between the headings pinned above and below. A heading in its place among the rows sits there as any row does, and is pinned only once its place leaves the visible rows. Clicking a pinned heading, anywhere but its chevron and controls, scrolls the list to that section's start; clicking its chevron expands or collapses it, as clicking a heading in its place does.
20:Each heading carries its section's controls, whichever place it is pinned in: Previous's selection, its "N selected", its batch actions, "Send N to Spec", "Send N to Code", and "Clear", while any task is selected, and its filter dropdown; Running's "Cancel all", while more than one task runs; and Queued's auto-send switch and "Send next". Where a heading is too narrow for all of them, its title gives way first, cut off with an ellipsis, and then its count, never its controls, the batch actions folding into a "N selected" menu once even that isn't enough.
22:The list's [Scrollbar](../../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) is pinned, as every scrollbar is: a column along the tab's right edge, always shown, whether or not the list has anything to scroll, running the tab's full height, from its top to its bottom, beside the pinned headings as well as the rows. It never scrolls with the list, never appears only while hovering or scrolling, and is never laid over the rows. The headings, pinned or in place, the day dividers, and every row end at the column's left edge, never running beneath it, so the column takes the same 18 pixels of width from all of them and their right-hand parts, the times and the headings' controls, line up against it. Its thumb is sized and placed from the whole list, the rows hidden beneath pinned headings and collapsed sections left out, so scrolling it to its bottom shows the last row whole. It has no lock to the bottom, since the list isn't output that keeps arriving.
31:Every task is one row, 28 pixels tall, as a queued prompt's is, and every row in every section is laid out in the same columns, so their parts line up down the whole list: a bar in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModes](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes) colours it, 4 pixels wide with corners rounded 2 pixels, inset from the row's edges, 4 pixels from its left and 6 from its top and bottom, so it stands as a short rounded pill rather than running edge to edge, and the bars of rows one above another never touch; then a lead column 20 pixels wide, holding a Previous row's checkbox, a Queued row's drag grip, and nothing in a Running row, the column kept empty rather than closed up where there is nothing in it; then a status column 20 pixels wide, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, or, queued, its place in the queue; then the first line of its prompt, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, how long it took, or has been running, as the [MessageList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) writes it, right-aligned in a column of its own, and any buttons the row has after it. So a row's status and its text start at the same place whether it has a checkbox, a grip, or neither, and so do the section headings' titles, set in from their chevrons to line up with the rows' text.
32:A chain, or any task of more than one step, is one row like any other, its status the chain's as a whole, with its step count muted beside its time. In Previous and Queued its steps are never listed in the list; they are shown once it is opened, as its chain steps say. While it is Running, it is expanded in the Running group: its row, then a row for each of its steps beneath it, in the order they run, sent or still to send, each a 28 pixel row in the same columns, its text set in 16 pixels further and labelled "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up" in that step's mode colour, with the step's own status, a tick, cross, or dash for one that has ended, a spinner for the one running, "Queued" with its place in its lane's queue for one waiting there, and a muted "Next" for one that will be sent once the step before it finishes, and "Waiting" for any after that, every step listed from the moment the chain is sent, as its chain steps say, each with its own time. A step being queued shows here, as part of its chain, rather than among the queued prompts, though it keeps its place in its lane's queue. The steps can't be collapsed, and once the chain is over they go with it into Previous as a single row. Clicking the chain's row, or any of its steps, opens the chain, its Steps section showing the same.
38:A row is drawn only from what its row shows, its mode, status, first line, and time, read from each task's history record once and kept, never by reading a record's output, lines, or snapshots while scrolling; those are read only when a task is opened. Running rows update their time and spinner in place, redrawing only what is in view. Scrolling to a row, as when the tab opens on Running, a filter changes, or a queued row is dragged past the edge, jumps straight to its place without drawing the rows between. A row scrolled out of view and back is the same as it was, its selection and highlight kept. A pinned heading sits over the list without moving any row, so where each row lies is unchanged by it.
39:Scrolling past either end does nothing: with the list at its top or its bottom, a wheel, trackpad, or drag that goes further leaves every row exactly where it is, frame after frame, with no stretch, bounce, or nudge of even a pixel and back, and draws nothing anew, since nothing moved. Its scroll position is clamped to its ends before a frame is drawn, never drawn past an end and corrected the frame after, and kept in whole device pixels, so a row never shimmers between two places. What lies at an end stays at it: a running row's time ticking, a task finishing, a row added or removed elsewhere in the list, or the tab being resized never makes the rows in view jump and settle. A list scrolled to its bottom stays at its bottom as rows are added, and one at its top stays at its top. The list counts as taller than the tab only once it overflows it by a whole pixel, as the right sidebar's panels do, so a list that fits never scrolls at all.
44:An open task takes the tab's place, with a back arrow and the task's mode and name along its top, the arrow and <Escape> going back to the list as it was left. Opening a task that has run or is running also opens it in a tab of its own in the body, as a file opens, as the [Body](../../../../scope/application/Body.md#body) says, showing its header and output there, unless it is a task the Chat tab shows, one running or the one it shows while none runs, when Chat is selected instead, with that task selected in its header. What the open task shows, top to bottom:
45:- Status: its status label and how long it took, or has been running, as the MessageList writes them, on one line
53:A queued task is edited right there: its prompt can be typed in, its attachments removed, and its parameters changed, its mode among those of the tabs, a change of lane moving it to that lane's queue in its place. Each change is saved with the project as it is made, as saving a queued prompt's edit is, and while it is being changed the task is held, never sent, as a queued prompt being edited is; going back, or opening another, lets it go. A task that has run, or is running, can't be changed: its prompt and parameters read as they were sent, and "Edit and resend" puts them in the open task as a new queued prompt, ready to change, sent once "Send" is clicked. The chat input's own <Up> editing still works as the [ChatInput](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) says, and opens the same task here.
57:An open Chain task lists its steps in its Steps section, beneath its prompt and above its details, in the order they run, each a row as in the list, with its status: its spec step, its code step, and its spec follow-up when it has one. Every step it will run is listed from the moment the chain is sent, while its spec step is still building or running, before any later step has been sent: a step not yet sent is listed all the same, its status a muted "Next" for the one that follows the step running and a muted "Waiting" for any after it, its prompt the chain's, and its time blank until it starts. Each step's row changes in place as the step is sent, queued, runs, and ends, and the list never grows or reorders as a step is sent, only once a step is added, or a spec follow-up is asked for, when it is added at its end. The same holds for the chain's expanded rows in the Running group, and for any task of more than one step. An "Add step" button beneath them adds a step of its own after the last: a Code or a Spec step, chosen from a small menu, with a prompt of its own, typed in the step's row as it expands, its model and effort those of the chain until changed. An added step runs once the step before it finishes, in its own mode's lane and place, as every step of a chain does, told its own prompt, the chain's prompt as typed, and what the step before it replied, as the spec-to-code prompt tells a code step, so a chain can be carried on, as a further code change once the spec is built, or a spec tidy-up after the code. A step not yet sent can be edited, moved among the others not yet sent, or removed; one sent reads as it was. Steps are saved with the chain, in its hidden anchor, as the [PromptSending](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending) keeps a queued prompt, so a chain keeps its added steps across restarts, and a step whose step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent, as none of a chain's are.
61:An open task that has started, and an open chain or step, has a Time section, beneath its Steps, or its Prompt where it has none, and above its Details, showing where its time went, so what is slow can be seen at a glance: waiting on the model, building the spec, running commands, and the rest.

content.text:
I found and fixed one real cause of chains being stuck in Running, but I can't see your task list. The sandbox blocks me from reading `.suspense`, so I can't confirm it's what your stale rows are.

**What I fixed:** when a chain's step finishes but the spec no longer builds, the chain waits on a "spec fix" task before sending its next step. If that fix was cancelled from the queue, or never made it into the queue, the chain was marked as waiting forever. It then stayed in Running for good, and it also held back its lane's queue. Now a chain counts as waiting only while its fix is actually running or queued. Cancelling a queued fix also releases the chain at once, so it shows as over.

The existing spec-fix test now covers the cancelled case and passes in a scratch copy.

**If stale rows remain after a restart:** tell me which ones, whether they're chains or single tasks, and their mode, or send a screenshot. Single tasks can't hit the bug above, so stale ones would point to a different cause.
